items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: And then Rufus Harley used to come to Buff — you ever heard of Rufus Harley? ... Rufus would come to town and he’d come up... So we have people like this you know.

ctx.x: Oh man. Did any of his — he would stand up for himself is one way to put it. He didn’t suffer fools gladly. Did you learn and observe that behavior and say this could be part of the way I need to operate on occasion?

Absolutely. I was — see when we were coming up in the ‘60s, especially when I was in high school as young artists, as young black men we were ready, there was a lot of that going on you know what I mean? A lot of assassinations were going on, there was a lot of protests and a lot of stuff was happening. And so we were looking for the right role models, you know, to want to be a part of this you know. And so we had people, Mingus was one of our main guys because he was a rebel, you know he wasn’t just accepting…
